item.title: A review of Last Interglacial sea-level proxies in South Asia and the Indian Ocean
item.dc:creator: Mubashir Ali, Ciro Cerrone, Alessio Rovere
item.description:
Earth System Science Data — matched: interglacial, last interglacial, proxy, sea level
We compiled a database of 54 ancient shoreline markers from Iran, Oman, India, the Maldives and the Cocos Islands, dating to Marine Isotopic Stage 5. The records show that the same past ocean level can appear far above today's sea on rising coasts, near today's level on stable coasts, and many meters underwater where land is sinking. This helps separate true ocean change from land motion and improves future sea-level planning.

item.title: Improving photosynthate allocation dynamic simulations of crops under water stress conditions
item.dc:creator: Wei Xu, Wen Zhang, Yongqiang Yu, Qing Zhang
item.description:
Geoscientific Model Development — matched: climate change
This study improves the Agro-C model to better represent how crops respond to changing soil moisture. The updated model adjusts carbon allocation between roots and leaves according to soil moisture and growth stage, and also accounts for leaf aging under water stress. Tests with field data for maize and wheat showed better predictions of plant growth above and below ground. The results can improve estimates of crop production and soil carbon storage under future drought and climate change.

item.title: A Lagrangian particle tracking framework for the super-droplet method in SCALE-SDM 5.2.6-2.3.1: implementation and computational evaluation
item.dc:creator: Chongzhi Yin, Shin-Ichiro Shima, Chunsong Lu
item.description:
Geoscientific Model Development
We developed and tested a way to trace selected cloud particles in a simulation, including how they grow and merge. One run identifies particles that meet chosen conditions, and a second reconstructs only their saved histories. In a three-dimensional test, the saved data were estimated to be one-fifth of what would be needed to keep all particle histories. Larger reductions are possible when fewer particles are selected, making such studies more practical in large simulations.

item.title: Development and validation of ARMS-gb v2.0: extending fast radiative transfer modeling capability to all-sky conditions for ground-based microwave radiometer retrievals
item.dc:creator: Ziyue Huang, Yi-Ning Shi, Fuzhong Weng, Jun Yang
item.description:
Geoscientific Model Development
Ground-based microwave instruments can continuously observe the lower atmosphere, but clouds make their measurements harder to use. We improved a computer model so that it represents how cloud and rain particles affect these observations, and tested it with six months of measurements from two sites in China. The updated model performed better under cloudy conditions without rain, supporting more reliable use of these observations in atmospheric monitoring and weather forecasting.
